title: Color / Duo’s palette
slide_intent: Connect colors to specific character parts because small inconsistencies can weaken recognition of a familiar mascot.
strategic_value: A body-part palette can help Duo look like the same character in print and on screens.
demonstration: Eleven named color cards provide values for wings, feathers, mask, beak parts, feet, tongue and neutrals, beside a consistency instruction.
practical_value: Use the named part-to-color mapping when preparing mascot artwork for a medium.

content_islands.name: Mascot color cards
content_islands.spec: Keep each named body-part or color swatch and its values in the left area.

content_islands.name: Consistency instruction
content_islands.spec: Place the heading and reminder about correct body-part colors in the right column.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source identifies Duo as the most recognizable brand asset and ties correct colors to consistent depiction.
reference_purposes.Application: Body-part names link colors to where they belong.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The source instructs users to use the right colors for each body part.

ingredient.name: Duo body-part palette
ingredient.role: Keep the mascot recognizable across reproductions.
ingredient.application: Use each supplied color for its named body part and retain the provided medium-specific values.
ingredient.scope: Historical archived guidelines. Historical Duo palette for screen and print. Do not substitute the general secondary palette for character parts.
